logreg.text: The cost of attending this university is outrageous. I don't know how I'm going to afford it.
I'm trying to graduate early but there are only a few courses available that I need to take. It's frustrating that my options are so limited.
I'm having trouble with a particular software program for one of my classes, but there's no one available to help me troubleshoot. It's frustrating to feel like I'm on my own.
I am struggling to find and access course materials needed for my classes due to limited availability in the library and online.
I wish there were more opportunities to access academic resources, such as extended library hours or online resources.
I'm not very good at managing my time, and it's been affecting my grades.
The cost of textbooks and other course materials is outrageous, and it's making it difficult to afford my education.
I'm constantly stressed about money and it's taking a toll on my academic performance.
I wish there were more scholarship opportunities available for students like me who don't come from wealthy backgrounds.
The stress of paying for college is causing me to lose sleep and focus on my studies.
The constant worry and stress about finances is taking a toll on my mental health.
I'm concerned about the quality of care I can receive with the limited insurance options available to me.
It's frustrating when people make assumptions about me based on my race or ethnicity, without taking the time to get to know me as an individual.
The lack of networking opportunities and professional development events for online students can be a major drawback.
The process for obtaining student certificates is unnecessarily complicated and time-consuming. It's taking away from my ability to focus on my studies.

I've been trying to update my personal information with the university, but the website keeps glitching and I can't get through to customer service. It's frustrating because this information is important for communication and academic purposes.

The university should provide more resources for students who are applying for internships and jobs. It's difficult to navigate the job market on your own, and career services is often understaffed and overworked.

I've had issues with financial aid and scholarships, and it seems like the university is always changing their policies and requirements. It's frustrating because I rely on this support to continue my education.
I've had to switch apartments multiple times because my landlord kept increasing the rent without warning. It's not fair for students who are already struggling to make ends meet.
I wish there were more affordable travel options for students. It's hard to justify spending a ton of money on a trip when we're already struggling to make ends meet with tuition and living expenses.
I'm struggling with mental health issues that are making it hard to focus on school. I'm working with a therapist to develop coping strategies.
I've been living on a tight budget since starting college and it's really stressful.
I feel like I'm drowning in debt and there's no way out.
I feel like I'm drowning in medical debt and can't see a way out.
I'm struggling to find a medication that works for me and doesn't break the bank.
Online students have limited access to internships and job opportunities, which puts them at a disadvantage compared to on-campus students.
As an online student, I feel like I'm missing out on internship and job opportunities that are only available to in-person students.

I recently applied for a scholarship through the university, but the application process was confusing and the instructions were unclear. It's frustrating to spend so much time on an application only to find out that I didn't meet the criteria.
The university should prioritize mental health resources for students. It's a stressful time in our lives and it's important to have access to counseling and support services when we need it.
I've had to resort to sleeping on a friend's couch because I can't afford the rent in the university area, and it's really taking a toll on my mental health.

I wish there were more opportunities for international students to get involved in leadership positions on campus. It would be a great way to develop our skills and contribute to the university community.
The limited access to online library resources and research databases made it hard to complete assignments and projects.
It's frustrating to have to rely on technology for my education, especially when it's not always reliable or user-friendly.

I received my training certificate from a course I took over the summer, but the university won't accept it because it's from a non-accredited institution. This is frustrating because the course was relevant to my major and I learned a lot from it.
The lack of available courses is making it hard for me to fulfill all of my degree requirements. I'm worried I won't be able to graduate on time.
I'm an international student and I'm having trouble accessing some of the online resources because of regional restrictions. It's frustrating to feel like I'm missing out because of where I'm from.
I'm a transfer student and I feel like I'm at a disadvantage because I don't have access to all of the same resources and databases as students who started at this university.
I wish there were more academic advisors available to provide guidance and support throughout my university experience.
Balancing my part-time job with my coursework has been a major struggle. I'm constantly exhausted and feel like I don't have enough time to focus on school.
It's frustrating that I have to work so many hours just to make ends meet, and it's taking away from my study time.
I've been trying to find a specialist for a specific medical condition, but it's been really difficult. There are limited options in my area and the ones that are available are really expensive.
It can be tough to balance the demands of academic work with the challenges of adapting to a new culture.

I've been feeling really burned out lately, and I think it's because I haven't had a chance to take a break and do something fun outside of class. I wish there were more social events and activities on campus that were geared towards stress relief and self-care.
I wish there were more opportunities to connect with other students who have similar interests. It can be tough to find a community of like-minded individuals on such a large campus.

I'm not really into partying or going out to bars, but it feels like that's the only social scene available on campus. I wish there were more options for students who want to have fun without drinking.
The course fees and textbook costs are way too high. I can barely afford to pay for everything and it's causing me a lot of stress.
I wish there were more opportunities for extra credit in this course. It would help my grade and encourage me to learn more.
I'm feeling burnt out and exhausted from the demands of my coursework. I'm trying to find ways to recharge and take care of my mental health.
I wish there were more opportunities for students to earn money through on-campus jobs.
I'm frustrated with the lack of transparency when it comes to how my tuition and fees are being spent by the university.

The cost of rent in this area is astronomical. I'm already working a part-time job just to make ends meet, and it's frustrating to feel like I'm barely scraping by even though I'm a full-time student.
I was really excited to go on a weekend trip with my friends, but the transportation ended up being a nightmare. Our bus broke down on the side of the road, and we ended up being stranded for hours.

I wish there were more opportunities to connect with alumni and professionals in my field. It would be great to network and get advice from people who have been through the same things I'm going through now.
